result.markdown: --- title: "Session 3 — Random-Intercept (Mixed) Models" subtitle: "Variance components · adjusted ICC · BLUPs and shrinkage · conditional vs marginal · Lab 3" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 2: keep an ordinary model and **repair the SE** - Today: **model the clustering** with a **random intercept** for village - By the end you can: - fit and read a **linear mixed model** with `lmer` - read **variance components** and the **adjusted ICC** - explain **shrinkage** of village estimates - contrast **conditional** and **marginal** effects ::: # Topic 1 — The model {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## A random intercept for each village ::: {.eq} SBP~ij~ = β~0~ + β~1~ Programme~j~ + β~2~ Age~ij~ + … + **u~j~** + ε~ij~ u~j~ ~ N(0, τ²), ε~ij~ ~ N(0, σ²) ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Fixed effects** β: the average relationship (the programme effect) - **Random intercept** u~j~: each village has its own shift, **drawn from a normal distribution** - τ² = **between-village** variance, σ² = **within-village** variance - ICC = **τ² / (τ² + σ²)** ::: ## Fit it ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m1 <- lmer(sbp ~ arm + age + sex + bmi + (1 | village), data = bp12) summary(m1)$coefficients |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Estimate Std. Error df t value Pr(>|t|) (Intercept) 105.469 4.503 638.117 23.423 0.000 armProgramme -3.565 1.602 39.036 -2.226 0.032 age 0.257 0.054 645.709 4.756 0.000 sexMale 3.014 1.131 639.770 2.665 0.008 bmi 0.363 0.145 641.818 2.506 0.012 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} The programme effect is **−3.6 mmHg** (SE **1.6**), with **Satterthwaite degrees of freedom of about 39** from `lmerTest`. `(1 | village)` means *a separate intercept for each village*. ::: ## Variance components and ICC ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} VarCorr(m1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Groups Name Std.Dev. village (Intercept) 3.6172 Residual 14.2415 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} icc(m1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # Intraclass Correlation Coefficient Adjusted ICC: 0.061 Unadjusted ICC: 0.056 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - Village SD **3.6** mmHg, residual SD **14.2** mmHg - **Adjusted ICC ≈ 0.06**: after accounting for age, sex, BMI and arm - Adjusted and unadjusted ICC differ because covariates explain part of the variance ::: ## Is the village effect needed? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ranova(m1) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` ANOVA-like table for random-effects: Single term deletions Model: sbp ~ arm + age + sex + bmi + (1 | village) npar logLik AIC LRT Df Pr(>Chisq) 7 -2689.2 5392.3 (1 | village) 6 -2695.2 5402.4 12.08 1 0.0005097 *** --- Signif. codes: 0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - A **likelihood-ratio** test of the random intercept: p ≈ **0.0005** - The test is on the **boundary** (τ² cannot be negative), so the p-value is conservative - **Do not drop** the cluster effect because the ICC is small or the test is not significant: the **design** says the data are clustered ::: # Topic 2 — Shrinkage {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Predicted village effects (BLUPs) ::: {.cell output-location='slide'} ```{.r .cell-code} tibble(village = rownames(ranef(m1)$village), re = ranef(m1)$village[, 1]) |> arrange(re) |> mutate(village = fct_inorder(village)) |> ggplot(aes(re, village)) + geom_point(colour = col_blue, size = 2.5) + geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2) + labs(x = "Predicted village shift (mmHg)", y = "Village") + theme(axis.text.y = element_blank()) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s3_mixed_models_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-5-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.key} Shifts range from about **−5 to +6 mmHg**. They are **predictions** (BLUPs), not parameters. ::: ## Shrinkage ::: {.eq} û~j~ = [ τ² / (τ² + σ²/n~j~) ] × (village mean − overall mean) ::: ::: {.incremental} - The factor is **between 0 and 1**: village estimates are **pulled towards the overall mean** - **Small** villages and **noisy** data are pulled **more**; large, precise villages less - Good for ranking or flagging villages: extremes by chance are **moderated** ::: # Topic 3 — Comparing approaches {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Same effect, three standard errors ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} rbind(naive = summary(m_lm <- lm(sbp ~ arm + age + sex + bmi, data = bp12))$coefficients["armProgramme", 1:2], cluster_robust = coeftest(m_lm, vcov = vcovCL(m_lm, cluster = bp12$village))["armProgramme", 1:2], mixed = summary(m1)$coefficients["armProgramme", 1:2]) |> round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Estimate Std. Error naive -3.42 1.15 cluster_robust -3.42 1.59 mixed -3.57 1.60 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} The **naive** SE is too small. The **cluster-robust** and **mixed-model** SEs agree. For a linear model with an identity link, the **conditional** and **marginal** effects are the **same**. ::: ## Conditional or marginal? | | Mixed model | GEE / robust | |---|---|---| | Effect | **Conditional**: same village | **Marginal**: average over villages | | Linear outcome | same number | same number | | Logistic outcome | **larger** odds ratio (further from 1) | smaller OR | | Also gives | village predictions, variance components | no cluster-level estimates | | Missing data | valid under MAR | needs more care | ## Reporting a mixed model ::: {.good} - State the **model**: fixed effects, the **random effect** and the **estimation** (REML) - Report the **effect with CI**, and say how the **df** were obtained - Report the **ICC** (adjusted) or the variance components - Say whether the effect is **conditional** ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 3 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `clustered-workshop/labs/lab3_mixed.R` - `lmer` with `(1 | village)` - variance components, ICC, `ranova` - BLUPs, a caterpillar plot and a comparison of SEs ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c3q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="47uf2b.85ck5m" data-show="QSBzaGlmdCBpbiBtZWFuIFNCUCBmb3IgZWFjaCB2aWxsYWdlLCBhc3N1bWVkIHRvIGZvbGxv dyBhIG5vcm1hbCBkaXN0cmlidXRpb24=" data-explain="VGhlIHJhbmRvbSBpbnRlcmNlcHQgaXMgYSB2aWxsYWdlLXNwZWNpZmljIGRldmlhdGlvbiBm cm9tIHRoZSBvdmVyYWxsIGludGVyY2VwdCwgZHJhd24gZnJvbSBhIG5vcm1hbCBkaXN0cmli dXRpb24gd2l0aCB2YXJpYW5jZSB0YXUgc3F1YXJlZC4="} In a model with (1 | village), what is the random intercept? - A shift in mean SBP for each village, assumed to follow a normal distribution - A separate fixed effect estimated for each of the forty villages in the study - The average SBP of the villages that were given the programme - The residual error of each adult measured within the study sample ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c3q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="47usb1.85cyn0" data-show="My42XjIgLyAoMy42XjIgKyAxNC4yXjIp" data-explain="VGhlIElDQyBpcyB0aGUgYmV0d2Vlbi1jbHVzdGVyIHZhcmlhbmNlIGRpdmlkZWQgYnkgdGhl IHRvdGFsIHZhcmlhbmNlLCBzbyBzcXVhcmVkIFNEcyBhcmUgbmVlZGVkOiAxMyAvICgxMyAr IDIwMiksIGFib3V0IDAuMDYu"} The village SD is 3.6 and the residual SD is 14.2. Which expression gives the ICC? - (3.6 + 14.2)^2 / 3.6^2 - 3.6^2 / (3.6^2 + 14.2^2) - 3.6 / (3.6 + 14.2)^2 - 14.2^2 / (3.6^2 + 14.2^2) ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c3q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="47v5js.85dd4f" data-show="SXQgcHVsbHMgdGhlIGVzdGltYXRlIHRvd2FyZHMgdGhlIG92ZXJhbGwgbWVhbiwgbW9yZSBz byBmb3Igc21hbGwgdmlsbGFnZXM=" data-explain="QkxVUHMgY29tYmluZSB0aGUgdmlsbGFnZSdzIG93biBkYXRhIHdpdGggdGhlIG92ZXJhbGwg bWVhbiwgd2l0aCBhIHdlaWdodCB0aGF0IGRlcGVuZHMgb24gaG93IG11Y2ggZGF0YSB0aGUg dmlsbGFnZSBoYXMuIExlc3MgZGF0YSBtZWFucyBtb3JlIHNocmlua2FnZS4="} What does shrinkage do to a village's predicted effect? - It moves the estimate further from the mean, which is stronger for small villages - It sets the village estimate to zero when the village has few adults in it - It drops from the model villages that have fewer than ten adults in them - It pulls the estimate towards the overall mean, more so for small villages ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c3q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="47vise.85drlp" data-show="S2VlcCB0aGUgY2x1c3RlciBpbiB0aGUgYW5hbHlzaXMsIHNpbmNlIHRoZSBkZXNpZ24gbWFr ZXMgZGF0YSBjbHVzdGVyZWQ=" data-explain="V2l0aCA1MCBwZXIgY2x1c3RlciwgREVGRiA9IDEgKyA0OSB4IDAuMDIgPSAyLiBUaGUgYW5h bHlzaXMgc2hvdWxkIGZvbGxvdyB0aGUgZGVzaWduLCBub3QgYSB0ZXN0IG9yIGEgc21hbGwg SUNDLg=="} An ICC of 0.02 is found in a cluster-randomised trial with 50 per cluster. What is the best action? - Keep the cluster in the analysis, since the design makes data clustered - Drop the cluster effect from the model, because an ICC this small is negligible - Drop the cluster effect once the ICC is shown to fall under a cut-off of 0.05 - Replace the cluster by a fixed effect for each person in the whole trial ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c3q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="47vw15.85e634" data-show="VGhlIGVzdGltYXRlcyBhcmUgY2xvc2UgYW5kIHRoZSBzdGFuZGFyZCBlcnJvcnMgYXJlIHNp bWlsYXI=" data-explain="V2l0aCBhbiBpZGVudGl0eSBsaW5rIHRoZSBjb25kaXRpb25hbCBhbmQgbWFyZ2luYWwgZWZm ZWN0cyBjb2luY2lkZSwgc28gdGhlIGVzdGltYXRlcyBhcmUgYWxpa2UsIGFuZCBib3RoIGFw cHJvYWNoZXMgZ2l2ZSBob25lc3QgU0VzLg=="} For a continuous outcome, how do the mixed model and cluster-robust lm effects compare? - The mixed model effect is about twice as large as the robust one - The cluster-robust SE is clearly smaller than the mixed model SE - The estimates are close and the standard errors are similar - They estimate different quantities and cannot be put side by side ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Random intercept** (1 | village): a normal shift per cluster - **ICC = τ² / (τ² + σ²)**; the adjusted ICC uses the model's variances - **BLUPs** are shrunk towards the mean - Keep the cluster effect because of the **design** - Linear model: conditional = marginal; not for logistic ::: **Next:** Session 4: repeated measures

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
